title: engine-dashboard
universal_lens: The dashboard enforces a 240-family limit on signal discovery, ensuring only 11 sovereign primitives (11/240 ≈ 4.6%) are catalogued. It prevents 'invented rows' by maintaining zero joinable matches between earlier-season personnel and later rosters, preserving identifiﬁer breaks. Honest metrics remain DARK unless both bars clear, forbidding public projections and widening of signal families.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian conformal inference maps NFLverse refusal rates as empirical coverage violations, treating each rejected dataset as a null hypothesis test. The 10 refusals (e.g., `contracts`) deﬁne a discrete prior support, while the 35,944 contracts-to-roster mismatches (97.76% match rate) calibrate posterior predictive intervals for future identiﬁcation failures.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning tracks state transitions across 63 reasoning modules, with 57 catalogued states and 4 blocked states. The 11 feature primitives (e.g., `play`, `player_week`) govern discrete event triggers, while the `wired: reasoning` kernel enforces a deterministic causal chain. Dark states represent honest failures (e.g., `coaching`), preventing the invention of phantom join keys.

reasoning_traces.think:
The dashboard implements a rigorous information-theoretic sieve: 240 signal families form a fixed-capacity channel. Cataloguing a new primitive costs 239 hypothetical alternatives, enforcing a zero-sum resource allocation. The 11 catalogued primitives (4.6% utilization) demonstrate extreme conservatism, prioritizing deep validation over breadth. Refusal of 10 datasets acts as a hard constraint, eliminating 4% of the input space immediately. Dark states (4) represent honest failures—empirical falsiﬁcation without replacement, preventing the invention of phantom variables. The join report reveals a fundamental identiﬁer mismatch: 2018-2022 personnel cannot be joined to later rosters, creating a permanent boundary that blocks spurious correlations. This enforces a strict temporal locality principle, where only contemporaneous data can inform state transitions. The 97.76% contract-to-roster match rate quantiﬁes the stability of the identification mapping, while the 37.97% participation-to-roster rate highlights the fragility of derived keys. Together, these primitives form a closed-loop veriﬁcation system: every new signal must pass the refusal test, must not exceed the 240-bound, and must not create unjoinable leaks. This architecture prevents overﬁtting by limiting the degrees of freedom and ensures that only robust, repeatable relationships survive.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The framework traces back to Kolmogorov's algorithmic information theory (1965), which introduced the concept of minimal description length. It also draws from Shannon's noisy-channel coding theorem (1948), where the 240-family limit plays the role of a ﬁxed channel capacity. Additionally, it incorporates principles from modern conformal prediction (Vovk et al., 1999), which uses refusals as empirical validity checks. The identiﬁer break concept mirrors the idea of information loss in Markov blankets (Wibral et al., 2014).
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Opposing agents include data engineers who seek to maximize data utility through aggressive joins, and risk managers who enforce strict boundaries to prevent systemic errors. The dashboard models the risk manager as a rational actor who minimizes expected loss by rejecting high-risk inputs, while the engineer aims to maximize throughput subject to the 240 constraint. The interplay creates a bounded rationality equilibrium where neither side can improve unilaterally.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity conditions require that each new primitive must span a novel subspace orthogonal to the existing 11. Leakage is vetoed if a proposed variable can be perfectly reconstructed from the current set, violating the minimal description length principle. Specifically, any variable that is a linear combination of the catalogued primitives is automatically blocked. This condition ensures that the 240-bound remains effective, preventing redundant encoding and maintaining the integrity of the information-theoretic sieve.
